title: Prices — base price and seasonal prices per room
body:
You reach the price module's settings screen on the Modules tab, with the **„Setting”** link next to the module.
You enter the price per room (per apartment) — this is also how the guest will see it on your site.
Every room has its own card.

![Screenshot: the price screen on a phone](assets/hu/screen.png)

## What is where on the screen?

The screen's title is the module's name: **„Prices, seasons”**. Above it is the **„Back to modules”** link, below the
title the module's fee and the **„Guide to this screen”** button (this help).

Below the introductory note is a row of small buttons: **„Where do guests see it?”**, the names of your rooms,
**„Meals”**, **„Rules”**. This row stays at the top of the screen while you scroll; tapping a button
jumps the page to that part, and the button for the part you are in is always highlighted.
On a computer the same list sits on the far right, with the **„On this page”** heading above it.

The parts of the page are arranged in groups, each with a small heading followed by a line running to the edge of the page:
**„Per-room prices”** (with the number of rooms next to it) — this is where the room cards are; and **„For the entire property”**
— here are Board and Rules. If you rent out the house only as one unit, the first group's heading is **„Whole-house price”**.

Below each room card's title, a line sums up what is set, for example “Base price 24,000 Ft · 2 seasons”;
as long as there is no base price, it reads **„No base price yet”**. Inside the card there are two pale blocks: **„Base price”** and
**„Seasonal rates”** — described below.

## Where do guests see your prices?

At the top of the screen, below the note, a box tells you where your prices currently appear on your
website. On the room cards, each room shows the price the guest sees (with several prices, the
lowest, marked “from”). The box lists these too.

A separate **price table** appears on the website only if it would say more than the cards. As long as every
room has only a base price, the table would repeat the same numbers one screen further down,
so in that case it does not appear — the box says so. The table appears by itself as soon as
you give any room a **seasonal price**, or fill in the **„Note on prices”** field at the bottom of the page.
Then the box says that your prices appear in two places, and tells you
why there is a table.

If a room has no price, the box names it in a yellow line starting with **„No price:”** — tapping the name
jumps to the room's card. There the yellow **„No price.”** line also says that the room's card on the website
will show no price, and that it will not be in the price table either.

## Base price

Type into the **„Base price”** field how much one night costs in this room, and tap the
**„Save”** button. This price applies whenever no seasonal price does — feel free to start
with just this; the rest can wait.

If you save with the price left empty, the price is removed from your site — better no number shown than
a wrong number.

## If you deliberately give no price

Some rooms you always price for the guest (how many are coming, for how long). In that case
tick the box below the base price: **„I won't set a base price — where there's no price, I'll send a custom quote”**.
The tick saves straight away; you do not need to press a separate button.

What happens next:

- For nights with no price, the guest sees no number and, instead of booking,
  **requests a quote**. You reply from the system (you get an email about the request). If the room
  has seasonal prices, the guest still sees the price in those periods.
- In the **„Pricing”** section of your site the room appears with the line “Based on an individual offer”. If it has
  seasonal prices, those apply, and the line “At other times” says that for the other
  nights you make an offer.
- You **get no reminders** about the room, and it does not appear among the tasks on the Overview either.

![Screenshot: a room without a price — the yellow line and the “I won't give a base price” box](assets/hu/nincs-ar.png)

A blue line on the card confirms: **„In short: no base price is set.”** You can withdraw it at any time by removing the
tick. If you enter a base price, the tick is removed by itself, since then every
night has a price. As long as there is a base price, the box is grey and cannot be ticked.

## If a room has no (complete) price

If a room has no price at all, or only for part of the year (for example only a high-season
price, without a base price), a yellow line on the card flags it: **„No price.”** or **„No price for part of the year.”**
In that case the guest sees no price for those nights and requests a quote. There are two
ways out: enter a base price, or tick that you deliberately give none. Until you do either,
we remind you by email every week.

The exception is the whole house when you rent it out room by room (“Rented as a whole only” is not ticked): nobody can book it
separately — anyone who wants the whole house selects every room — so we do not ask for a price for it:
no yellow line, no task, no reminder.

## “Base price, with dates” — a price saved from a quote

If, for a quote, you tick the **„Save to the price list too?”** box with the **„Only for the requested days”**
option, the price appears on the room's card as an **„Base price, with date”** line, with the
dates. It applies only to the nights the guest requested (where there is no seasonal price), and after the stay
it is removed by itself — your website is updated too. That is why **we send no expiry
email** about this price: after it expires, no future night is left without a price because of it. You can remove the line at any time
with the **„Delete”** button.

About seasonal prices we write at the end of the season (see below: **Email at the end of the season**): there we ask
what the price should be next year.

## Seasonal prices (e.g. high season)

In the **„Seasonal rates”** section you can set different prices for parts of the year:

1. Type a name into the **„Period name”** field (e.g. High season).
2. Under **„From–to”**, tap the **„Start”** button: a calendar opens. Tap the
   first day, then the last day — the calendar then closes by itself. You can move between months with the two
   arrows. The calendar has no year, because the season applies on the same days every
   year; you do not have to enter it again in January.
3. Type the price into the **„Price / night”** field, and tap the **„Add”** button.

Below the fields we spell out what your choice means — from which day to which day it applies every
year, and when it comes round next. In the calendar, the days of the room's other seasons are underlined
in yellow, so you can see where they would overlap. Below it, the **„The year at a glance”** strip shows the whole
year: the new season in blue, the existing ones in yellow. Tapping one of its months jumps the calendar there.

![Screenshot: the calendar opened by the “Start” button below the new season's fields](assets/hu/naptar.png)

**A season spanning the end of the year** (e.g. winter low season from November to March): choose the
first day in November, then page forward and choose the last day in March. In that case
the fields and the line show the **„extends past year-end”** mark. The years then get two
year numbers, for example 2026/27.

### The name: use the same as for the other rooms

If you tap the name field and the property already has seasons, a list of the names used so far drops down. Under **„Previously used names”**
are the seasons of the property's other rooms, with their days and which
room uses them. The list narrows as you type. If you choose a name, we copy its days
as well — if they fall on other days for this room, tap the date and change it. The
names under **„This room already has”** cannot be chosen: you can edit that season in the list
above.

If you write a name slightly differently from before (e.g. in lower case or without accents), we point it out
below the field, and you can unify it with one button — so the guest's price table does not show two “high seasons”
one under the other. Two seasons of the same room cannot have the same name.

### Changing a season

With the **„Edit”** button next to the line you can change the name, the days and the price — if you
also have online booking, the minimum too —, then **„Save”** (or **„Cancel”**). Here too you choose the days in the
calendar; if you only want to change the last day, it is enough to tap the **„End”** button. Separate prices set for individual years are kept.

You remove a season with the **„Delete”** button — the separate prices set for its years go
with it, and the base price applies there again. If there is no seasonal price at all, the
base price always applies.

### If two seasons fall on the same day

Where two seasons overlap (e.g. the “Winter price” from November to February, and “Holidays” within it), the
price of the season **higher up the list** counts. You can reorder them with the small up and down arrows in front of the
**„Edit”** button. If a new or changed season overlaps another, a yellow
line below the fields tells you whose price will apply on the shared days.

## A different price in a given year

Below every season are the years, each on a card (starting from the nearest year that has not yet
passed). Swiping sideways — or using the two arrows — takes you to further years, as far ahead as you like.

- If you want something different in a year (e.g. high season will be more expensive next year), type the price on that year's
  card and tap the **„Save”** button. The card then gets the **„custom price”** mark.
- Where you type nothing, **„the recurring price”** applies — nothing breaks if you do not give
  a separate price.
- The **„Back to recurring”** button deletes that year's separate price.
- If the season falls on different days in a year (e.g. Easter, or you rent from Saturday to Saturday),
  tap the **„On other days this year”** caption on the card. A calendar opens below the year strip
  — this one shows the year and the days of the week. Choose the first and the last day; below,
  we show which weekdays they fall on and how many days it is. Tap the **„Save days”** button. After that the
  card says “own days”, and you can change the days under **„Edit days”**. This
  applies only to that one year; the other years do not change.

![Screenshot: a year's own days in the calendar, with the year and the days of the week](assets/hu/ev-naptar.png)

On your website we show the year only if that season has a separate yearly price — in that case
the guest sees the price year by year for the bookable months.

### Email at the end of the season

On the morning after a season's last day we send you an email: what its price was this year, and what it
should be next year. If it stays the same, you do not have to do anything. If you want to change it, the email's link takes you straight to
the next year's card — if it asks you to log in first, it takes you there after logging in too. We write about a season once a year, and we do not write if you have
already set a price for the following year.

## When you rent it out, and for at least how many nights — with online booking

These two settings affect the **booking calendar**, so they only appear if the Online
booking module is switched on as well:

- **„At least”** — in the new season's line, next to the price: in this season bookings must be for at least this many
  nights (e.g. 3 in summer). It is optional: if you leave it empty, the shortest booking set in the Online booking
  module applies. In an existing season's line you see what you entered below the price.
- **„Only available during the listed periods”** — a switch at the bottom of the room's card.
  When it is on, the guest cannot even select days outside the listed seasons in the calendar
  (e.g. you are closed in winter). When it is off, the room can be booked all year, and the seasons only
  fine-tune the price and the minimum. It can be set separately for each room.

If you have no online booking, the guest sends a date request, and you decide on it — in that case these
two have no effect, so you do not see them. In their place a short line says what booking
would add. If you set them earlier, while you had booking, they are not lost: without booking they are
paused (they do not close your calendar shared with the portals either), and if you switch
booking back on, they carry on working just as before.

Online booking is a separate module with a monthly fee. The **„Online booking”** link below the line takes you to the Modules
tab; there, in the **„Add-ons — what else you can add”** section, find the Online booking
card — it also shows the monthly fee —, and tap the **„Add to cart”** button.

## Several rooms, several prices

If you have several rooms, you can price each on its own card — the apartment facing the garden can cost more
than the attic room. If you have not added your rooms yet (for example, so far only “The entire property” appears,
but you want to rent room by room), do that first in the room module; the pricing sees the same rooms.
You do not have to search: at the top of the screen, below the introductory text (beside it on a computer), the **„Edit rooms and apartments”**
button takes you straight to the room module's settings screen. If the Rooms module is not switched on
yet, the button reads **„Enable Rooms module”** and takes you to the Modules tab — there, on the
Rooms, apartments card, put it in your basket with the **„Add to cart”** button and finalise it in the basket; after that the button points to the
editor.

![Screenshot: the introductory line at the top of the screen, with the “Edit rooms, apartments” button below it](assets/hu/szobak-gomb.png)

## The whole house's price — only if you rent it out as one unit

**If you rent it out room by room** (this is the default), you do not need to give the whole house a price. In one request the guest can
select several rooms, even all of them, and pays the prices of the selected rooms: when booking they see them item by item
per room, with the total below. So it is enough to price the rooms — in that case the house has
no separate card on this screen, only the rooms do.

**If you rent it out only as one unit** (in the Rooms, apartments module, on the **„The whole house”**
card above the grid, **„Rented as a whole only”** is ticked), then only the whole house can be booked, and
we ask for a price only for the house. You can enter it here, on the house's card, or on the Rooms module's
**„The whole house”** card, below the **„Base price:”** line (with the **„Save price”** button). In that case the rooms
are shown for display only, so they have no card here. If the house has no price, the guest
requests a quote.

## Board — breakfast, half board, full board

Below the room cards, in the **„Meals”** section, you set what the price includes and what the
guest can request for a supplement. The setting applies to every room; you can exclude rooms where it is not available.

![Screenshot: the Board section on a phone](assets/hu/ellatas.png)

1. **„What's included in the base price?”** — choose: *Room only*, *Breakfast*, *Half board* or
   *Full board*. The room prices (above) are understood with this. Anything less than this cannot be offered
   (there is no negative supplement), so it disappears from the table too.
2. **„Optional board”** — tick what you offer, and type in its supplement. Next to it,
   in the **„For what”** column, choose whether the price is **per person / night** or **per room / night**. Tapping the **„What's included?”** link
   lets you add a short description (e.g. *breakfast and dinner, drinks not included*) — the guest reads this
   too. If you tick a board option but type no supplement, saving does not go through, and the field
   turns red: nothing is saved until you correct it.
3. **Child price** — in the **„For a child”** column you can enter a separate, cheaper price (0 means:
   free), and below it you **must** state up to what age someone counts as a child (between 1 and
   17) — without it, saving does not go through. Where the child price is empty, a child pays the adult
   price too. The child price only counts where the price is **per person / night**; with the **per room / night** price the number of people does not
   matter, so this field does not even appear there. When booking, the guest states how many are children.
4. **„Which rooms offer meals?”** (only if you have several rooms) — untick the room where board is not available.
   There the guest sees no board choice, only that board cannot be requested for this accommodation. If the guest
   requests several rooms at once and board is available for only some of them, the supplement counts only for those
   rooms (the guest sees which ones), and about the others they read: “Board not available for:” and the rooms' names.
5. **„What else is included in the price?”** — in your own words (e.g. *cleaning, bed linen, towels*).
   The guest reads it with the rooms and when booking, below the itemised price. If left empty, it is omitted.

Tap the **„Save”** button at the bottom of the Board section. A **„Meals”** section with the supplements appears on your website,
when booking the guest chooses from a drop-down, and sees the board on a separate line in the itemised price.
The chosen board also appears on the booking request (on the **Bookings** tab as a tag, itemised when you tap the
**„Price breakdown”** line, and in the email too), recorded together with the supplement — if you change the prices later, a request already received does not
change.
